en.title: Number of Subsequences Greater Than the System Password
en.description:
Choose a subsequence of the customer password s by index, and count the choices that are lexicographically strictly greater than t, modulo 1000000007. When the same resulting string comes from different index choices, each is counted separately.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: Two lines, s and t; 1≤|s|≤100000, 1≤|t|≤100, both lowercase.
en.explanation: Example 1: the three choices b, ba and aba are strictly greater, so the answer is 3. Example 2: the two b's at different positions plus ba, bb and bab, 5 in total. Example 3: only the full aaa is greater than aa, so the answer is 1.
hints: Let dp[j] count the subsequences currently equal to exactly the first j characters of t, and let greater count the choices that are already strictly greater. A new character can extend a greater state, or become greater at the first point of difference; update match lengths from back to front to avoid reusing a position.
